context_notes: AliExpress ship-to was set to Canada / Ontario / Toronto, currency CAD. All AliExpress prices are CAD, tax excluded (HST is added at checkout).
Many AliExpress 'welcome deal' prices are for new shoppers only, often limited to 1 per shopper. Where a listing showed one, the strikethrough regular price is also recorded.
Main finding: the cheap prices Kimi quoted for items 1-3 are the price of the default variant (bracket only, or the FE-URT2 board only), not the servo.

Amazon.ca: the logged-in session's 'Deliver to' is set to Santa Clara 95051 (USA). Because of that, most Amazon.ca listings showed 'Currently unavailable' and hid the Buy Box price. The only prices shown were the 'N options from $X' on variation tiles, or Amazon US import listings. Amazon stock is therefore UNVERIFIED for a Toronto address. I did not change the delivery location because it is shared with the user's active cart tab.
WebFetch of amazon.ca returned only page scaffolding with no product data.

rows.kimi_claim: Exists, iOS HEBI / Android WebXR; one phone drives one arm
rows.specs_seen: pip install lerobot[phone]. iOS uses the HEBI Mobile I/O app (ARKit). Android uses the 'teleop' PyPI package (WebXR via a local URL). Examples are in examples/phone_to_so100 (teleoperate/record/replay/evaluate) with the SO101 URDF so101_new_calib.urdf. Control is end-effector IK via Placo. The config is a single PhoneConfig with one robot.
rows.note: Supports SO-100/SO-101 follower on iOS and Android. The page does NOT mention bimanual control or multiple phones; every example is one phone to one arm. Bimanual would need custom code running two Phone teleops. Kimi is right that one phone drives one arm.
